meta.title: HAB-1 hindcast, 31 October 2026
meta.what: The predictor (boscon-hab-predictor, src/physics unchanged) re-run on the GFS winds for the actual day and release time, with the pre-flight settings and with the as-flown ascent, burst and descent.
meta.code: boscon-hab-predictor src/physics/predictor.ts planFill, buildFlightConfig and flyWithTerrain (trajectory.ts flyTrajectory, RK4, 5 s step); winds by src/data/openmeteo.ts fetchGridField; ground by fetchElevations. Run headless through Vitest (import.meta.env resolves) from a script outside the repo; no predictor file was changed.

winds.source: Open-Meteo forecast API (https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast), models=gfs_seamless, the predictor's own fetch
winds.model: NOAA GFS 0.25 deg as served by Open-Meteo, 23 pressure levels 1000 to 10 hPa plus 10/80/120/180 m above-ground winds
winds.label: NOAA GFS via Open-Meteo (0.25°, 23 levels to 10 hPa ≈ 31 km), data 2026-10-31T06:00Z..2026-10-31T15:00Z
winds.grid: 9 x 9 columns, 0.25 deg spacing, pad +/- 1.0 deg (lat 16.7142 to 18.7142, lon 74.8295 to 76.8295), hourly 2026-10-31T06:00:00.000Z onward
winds.which_run: assumed: for hours already past, Open-Meteo serves the short-lead value of the latest GFS run covering each hour, not the 01:38 UTC run the pre-flight prediction used. A spot request at the pad (4 variables, 06 to 10 UTC) returned identical numbers from api.open-meteo.com and historical-forecast-api.open-meteo.com (measured, 2026-11-01).

pad.source: measured, beacon GPS last pad fix (10-flight-report.md). The pre-flight run used the NOTAM point 17 43 18 N, 075 50 33 E at 509.11 m, 1.6 km away (computed); this hindcast uses the actual pad for every scenario.

meta.ground: Ground height at landing from the Open-Meteo elevation API (Copernicus GLO-90), the predictor's fallback when no Mapbox token is loaded (none is, headless); refined up to 3 times at the landing point by flyWithTerrain. The flight report computes about 634 m at the real touchdown.

units.path: [t_s since release, lat_deg, lon_deg, alt_m AMSL], every 10 s of model time plus the burst and landing points
units.range_km,miss_*_km: km, great circle on a 6371.009 km sphere (predictor geo.ts)
units.bearing_deg: deg true from the pad (miss_bearing_deg: from the actual touchdown to the modelled landing)
units.impact_ms: m/s, modelled descent rate at the ground

meta.kinds: Every scenario number is COMPUTED by the model. Inputs are labelled measured, predicted (pre-flight) or assumed in each scenario's settings.
meta.decomposition: preflight -> as_flown_preflight_descent changes only ascent rate and burst height; as_flown_preflight_descent -> as_flown changes only the descent. Ranges (computed): 42.8 -> 49.7 -> 60.3 km; distance from the actual touchdown: 22.7 -> 13.3 -> 4.1 km.
not_done: No Monte Carlo was run for the hindcast; each scenario is one deterministic track.
A pre-flight ascent with the measured descent table was not used: the table exists only up to 19.6 km and cannot be extended to a 30 km burst without assuming a descent law.
The as-flown ascent is a constant 4.54 m/s; the measured rate varied 3.96 to 5.04 m/s by 1 km band (computed, Pi log), not modelled.
The cause of the slow descent (chute Cd, balloon remnants or both) is not separated; the table just reproduces the measured rates.

The 25 and 30 km burst what-ifs hold the constant 4.54 m/s ascent above 19.6 km and extrapolate the fitted sea-level descent law above 19.6 km; neither was measured there. Each is one deterministic track, no Monte Carlo.
meta.what_if_bursts: burst_25km and burst_30km: as_flown_sl_fit with only the burst height changed, same GFS fetch (as_flown and as_flown_sl_fit re-flown in the same run and matched sim.json exactly, computed 2026-11-01). Script: hab1-launch/tools/sim/bursts.test.ts.

actual.source: flight-details/31-oct-26-landing/sd/hab1/boot-0027 (Pi log, beacon GPS at 1 Hz) and 10-flight-report.md
actual.track_note: measured GPS, sampled every 10 s from the 1 Hz Pi log; [t_s since release, lat, lon, GPS alt m]
actual.descent_rate_note: measured_ms is computed from the Pi 1 Hz GPS: band height / time between first crossings of its top and bottom on the way down; the bottom band runs from the about 634 m ground to 1 km and uses the 09:11:45Z touchdown time. preflight_model_ms is the pre-flight descent law (2.3 kg, 1.2 m, Cd 0.75) in the 31 Oct GFS density column at the band centre (computed). The flight report's coarser figures (9.98 at 18 to 20 km, 6.52 at 8 to 10, 4.92 at 4 to 6, 3.54 at 2 to 4 km) come from the ground-station CSV.

settings.ascent: predictor default fill and Gallice drag model: Pawan CPR-1200, hydrogen, 2.0 kg payload (assumed in the pre-flight, not weighed), filled for 5.0 m/s at the pad (neck lift 3.102 kg, computed)
settings.burst_source: computed by planFill (burst diameter of the CPR-1200 spec), predicted 30.1 km pre-flight
settings.descent: 1.2 m chute, Cd 0.75 on nominal area, 2.3 kg under the canopy (2.0 kg payload + 0.3 kg remnant, the predictor default, assumed); v = sqrt(2 m g / (rho Cd S0)) in the GFS density column: 6.59 m/s at sea-level density, 6.97 m/s at the pad (computed)

as_flown.label: As flown: measured ascent, burst and descent rates

settings.ascent: constant 4.54 m/s (computed mean, measured release and burst)
settings.descent: measured descent-rate table (actual.descent_rate_bands): rate at each band centre, linear in altitude between centres, held beyond the end centres. Fed to the unchanged integrator through an input adapter: the descent config is m = 1 kg, D = 1 m, Cd = 1 and the atmosphere handed to flyTrajectory returns, at each altitude, the density that makes the predictor's terminal-velocity formula equal the table rate. Winds are untouched (the adapter only wraps the density; with a constant ascent rate density is used for nothing else).

as_flown_sl_fit.label: As flown, descent as one fitted sea-level rate

settings.descent: predictor seaLevelRate mode (fromSeaLevelRate), v = v_sl sqrt(rho_sl / rho), with v_sl = 3.44 m/s fitted by least squares to the 20 measured band rates using the 31 Oct GFS density column (computed); RMS misfit 0.82 m/s over the bands, so one sea-level rate does not fit this descent well (the measured profile is flatter than sqrt(1/rho))

as_flown_preflight_descent.label: Measured ascent and burst, pre-flight descent

settings.descent: the pre-flight chute model, as in preflight

burst_25km.label: What if: as flown, burst at 25 km

settings.ascent: constant 4.54 m/s (computed mean, measured release and burst), held to the assumed burst height
settings.burst_source: assumed, a what-if; HAB-1 burst at 19,624.8 m (measured)
settings.descent: as in as_flown_sl_fit: predictor seaLevelRate mode, v = v_sl sqrt(rho_sl / rho), v_sl = 3.44 m/s fitted to the 20 measured band rates (computed); 19.07 m/s at the burst height in the GFS density column (computed). Above 19.6 km this law is extrapolated, not measured.

burst_30km.label: What if: as flown, burst at 30 km

settings.ascent: constant 4.54 m/s (computed mean, measured release and burst), held to the assumed burst height
settings.burst_source: assumed, a what-if; HAB-1 burst at 19,624.8 m (measured)
settings.descent: as in as_flown_sl_fit: predictor seaLevelRate mode, v = v_sl sqrt(rho_sl / rho), v_sl = 3.44 m/s fitted to the 20 measured band rates (computed); 28.78 m/s at the burst height in the GFS density column (computed). Above 19.6 km this law is extrapolated, not measured.

preflight_table.source: hab1-launch/docs/07-launch-readiness.md section 0.15, verbatim (predicted, run at 07:10 IST on 31 Oct; GFS run generated 01:38 UTC; NOTAM launch point)
